prompt:
I teach a biostatistics class. I need a Shiny app where students upload a CSV (chick_weights.csv is an example of the kind of file they'll use), pick a numeric column and a grouping column from dropdowns that fill in from the uploaded file, see summary stats per group (n, mean, sd, missing values) and a boxplot, and then download a short HTML report with the table and the plot. Some files will have missing values. Make it in a folder upload_app.

Input files: chick_weights.csv
assertions: Running the skill's scripts/check_app.R on the produced app directory reports 0 errors.
Column dropdown choices are filled from the uploaded file's columns (updateSelectInput/updateSelectizeInput or renderUI), with the numeric dropdown limited to numeric columns.
Code reads input$<file>$datapath and guards with req() so nothing errors before a file is uploaded.
Summary statistics use na.rm = TRUE (or equivalent) and report a per-group count of missing values; on chick_weights.csv the weight column shows 6 missing in total.
When the report download is triggered with chick_weights.csv uploaded (e.g. via testServer), an HTML file is produced that contains the summary table and an embedded plot.
The report is rendered from a template copied to tempdir() (or otherwise not written into the app folder) and receives data via params or an explicit environment, not via global variables.
Uploading a CSV that has no numeric column shows a readable message in the page (validate/need, showNotification or similar that is actually displayed) rather than a blank page or an R error.
Uploading a file that is not a CSV (e.g. a .txt with random text, or wrong extension) produces a readable message and no R error.
